solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: In favour of disco becoming rhythmical

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: becoming signals that the word disco turns into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone approves of disco music turning rhythmic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becoming' rearranges DISCO into SODIC, placed after PRO.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosody is the study of metre, so prosodic describes rhythmical patterns in verse.

clue.text: Sound comment distinguishing mark on etching

indicators.note: Sound tells us the following word is to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: a comment is a remark

explanation.surface: A remark that sounds right about an identifying mark on a print.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' signals that REMARK, spoken, gives the French-spelt REMARQUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Technical term: a small sketch or mark in an etching's margin that identifies the proof state.

clue.text: No growth in all-male country

parts.note: a stag party is an all-male gathering, so stag can mean all-male
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: An all-male country would have no population growth.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnation is a lack of development or growth, especially in an economy.

clue.text: Hide one's kid playing

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of one's kid are frolicking about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone's child is playing hide and seek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges the seven letters of ONE'S KID.
explanation.definitionFit: Doeskin is the hide of a female deer, a soft leather.

clue.text: Many a nobleman getting up will advance slowly

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many

indicators.note: in a down clue getting up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a peer is a nobleman

explanation.surface: A crowd of aristocrats rising from their seats will move forward slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting up' turns PEER into REEP, after C; 'will' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: To creep is to move forward slowly and quietly, inching along.

clue.text: Sure Tay meanders into it

indicators.note: a river that meanders wanders about, so the letters of Sure Tay wander into a new order

explanation.surface: The River Tay surely winds its way down to the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meanders' rearranges SURE TAY. The whole clue also defines: the Tay, a Scottish river, flows into the Firth of Tay, its estuary.
explanation.definitionFit: An estuary is the tidal mouth where a river flows into the sea.

clue.text: Brief details about upper-class standing

indicators.note: about means the details go around the upper-class letter

parts.note: stats, short for statistics, are details in brief

explanation.surface: Short facts concerning someone's high social rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts U inside STATS.
explanation.definitionFit: Status and standing both mean someone's position or rank in society.

clue.text: Turned out I had gone round having entered uninvited

indicators.note: gone round means I had encircles the rest

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had

indicators.note: out tells us the word Turned is put out of order

explanation.surface: It emerged that I had walked round, having come in without being asked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges TURNED into NTRUDE; 'gone round' puts ID around it.
explanation.definitionFit: To intrude is to enter where one is not invited, so the past tense fits.

clue.text: Puritan's becoming a monk

indicators.note: becoming signals that the letters of Puritan's change into something else

parts.note: the letters of Puritan's, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A Puritan is turning into a monk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becoming' rearranges PURITANS. Rasputin was the Russian mystic, often described as a monk, at the court of the last Tsar.
explanation.definitionFit: Grigori Rasputin was a Russian holy man commonly called the mad monk.

clue.text: Transfix victim, pal entrenched inside

indicators.note: inside says the answer lies within the run of letters of victim, pal entrenched

explanation.surface: A victim is pierced while a friend is dug in nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' points to the letters spanning victIM PAL Entrenched.
explanation.definitionFit: To impale is to pierce through with a stake, to transfix.

clue.text: Second embezzler is better

parts.note: a peculator is one who embezzles public money

explanation.surface: A second embezzler is an improvement on the first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' looks like a comparative adjective; it is a noun, one who bets.
explanation.definitionFit: A speculator takes financial gambles, so is a kind of punter or bettor.

clue.text: Tanks of water reaching valley

parts.note: aqua is Latin for water
a ria is a long narrow drowned river valley

explanation.surface: Water containers stretching into a valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' and 'reaching' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquaria is the plural of aquarium, glass tanks for keeping fish.

clue.text: One fragment, one artery

parts.note: a means one
an ort is a scrap or fragment of food
a means one again

explanation.surface: A single piece, a single blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the main artery leaving the heart.

clue.text: How iron was put into service?

definitions.meaning: describing what an iron did to clothes: flattened them smooth
forced into service, as press gangs did to sailors

explanation.surface: Asking how a metal was conscripted.
explanation.walkthrough: Press gangs forcibly enlisted men into the Royal Navy in the 18th century.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes are pressed by an iron, and men were pressed, impressed, into naval service.

clue.text: Attorney's force?

definitions.meaning: what an attorney holds, as in the legal authority granted to act for another

explanation.walkthrough: A power of attorney is a document authorising someone to act on another's behalf.
explanation.definitionFit: Power means strength or force, and an attorney exercises a legal power.

clue.text: Lullabies?

parts.note: playfully, songs for bedtime are tunes for the bedclothes, music of the linen

explanation.walkthrough: The bed sheet pun: lullabies are music for going under the sheets.
explanation.definitionFit: Printed scores are this; whimsically, bedtime songs suit the sheets of a bed.

clue.text: Without success when lady's not there

definitions.meaning: read literally, a woman's name is absent: none of her present

explanation.surface: Getting nowhere when the woman fails to turn up.
explanation.walkthrough: Joy is a woman's name, so the second reading says no woman called that is present.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for failing to get anywhere with an attempt is to have none of this.

clue.text: Before nine, umpire put things right again

indicators.note: Before tells us the umpire comes ahead of the nine

parts.note: ref, short for referee, is an umpire
IX is nine in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An umpire sorted matters out before nine o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' places REF ahead of IX.
explanation.definitionFit: To refix something is to mend or fasten it once more.

clue.text: Crowd taking wine from hiker's bag

parts.note: a ruck is a crowd or throng
sack is an old name for a dry white wine like sherry

explanation.surface: A crowd taking wine out of a walker's pack.
explanation.walkthrough: SACK, the old Spanish wine, is also a bag, which strengthens the surface. 'taking' and 'from' join.
explanation.definitionFit: A rucksack is a bag carried on the back by walkers.

clue.text: He had a right inside to be listened to

indicators.note: inside means a right goes into He had

parts.note: he'd is the contraction of he had

explanation.surface: A man was entitled to have his say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts AR into HED; 'to be' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Heard is the past participle of hear, so it means listened to.

clue.text: Restore said bird with egg-shaped behind!

indicators.note: said shows the bird's name is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a wren is a small bird
ovate means egg-shaped

explanation.surface: A bird with an oval rear is told to restore itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' gives WREN as heard, REN; 'with ... behind' puts OVATE after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To renovate is to restore something to good condition.

clue.text: Mainly bewildered?

parts.note: the main is the open ocean, so being on the main suggests a sailor afloat, while the phrase also means confused

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mainly' is not 'mostly' here: the main is the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for confused is literally being out on the ocean.

clue.text: Joining confederate at home before midnight

indicators.note: before places the earlier pieces ahead of the midnight letter

parts.note: a confederate is an ally
in means at home
the middle of the word night, its centre letter, read as mid night

explanation.surface: Joining a partner at home before the clock strikes twelve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'midnight' is split: the middle of 'night' is G.
explanation.definitionFit: Allying means joining together in an alliance.

clue.text: Eggplant not in the inn

indicators.note: not means the following word is removed

parts.note: aubergine is the British word for eggplant

explanation.surface: Aubergine isn't on the menu at the hostelry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes IN from AUBERGINE; 'the' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Auberge is the French word for an inn, used in English too.

clue.text: Tube may damage ulna

parts.note: can and may both express permission or possibility

indicators.note: damage suggests the word ulna is broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: A tube might harm a forearm bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damage' rearranges ULNA into NULA, after CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A cannula is a thin tube inserted into the body to drain or deliver fluid.

clue.text: How one had given a pointed reminder

definitions.text: How one had given a pointed reminder

parts.words: How one had given a pointed reminder
parts.note: describes prodding someone with an elbow to jog their memory

explanation.definitionFit: A gentle push with the elbow serves as a hint, so the past tense fits a reminder already given.

clue.text: Acquiring a reddish-brown coat

parts.note: sounds like a dog or horse growing a chestnut coat, but describes metal corroding

explanation.definitionFit: Iron oxidising develops a reddish-brown layer of corrosion.

clue.text: Piece about last character on point of becoming composer

indicators.note: about means piece is wrapped around the other letters

parts.note: a bit is a piece
Z is the last character of the alphabet
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A fragment about the final letter on the verge of turning into a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts Z and E inside BIT; 'on' and 'of becoming' join.
explanation.definitionFit: Georges Bizet was the French composer of the opera Carmen.

clue.text: 11-11 abreast?

parts.note: eleven players make a team in football or cricket, so each eleven is a side, the two standing next to each other

explanation.surface: Two numbers placed next to one another.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 is not a cross-reference: a football or cricket team of eleven is a side, and the hyphen sets one beside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Side by side means next to each other, abreast.

clue.text: Oriental sailor changed sides, the rogue

indicators.note: sides here are left and right, L and R, so they trade places

parts.note: a lascar is a sailor from India or Southeast Asia

explanation.surface: An Asian seaman defected and turned out to be a villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed sides' swaps the L (left) and R (right) in LASCAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal is a mischievous rogue or scamp.

clue.text: Belief about colour in French church

parts.note: C, circa, means about
red is a colour
en is French for in
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Faith concerning colour inside a French church.
explanation.definitionFit: Credence means belief or trust in something being true.

clue.text: At mealtimes this man will dig in

definitions.text: At mealtimes this man will dig in

parts.words: At mealtimes this man will dig in
parts.note: a hearty eater tucks in, but one who cuts ditches also digs; a wooden platter for food carries the same name

explanation.definitionFit: Literally one who digs ditches, and also an old wooden plate used at meals.
